source.title: Revised6 Report on the Algorithmic Language Scheme — Standard Libraries (2007)

ownership: Candidate language-observable table-copy and mutability capabilities; prove independent irreducible root versus selected MAKE-HASH-TABLE/GETHASH and value identity prior to canonical selection. No D2 change or T5 authority.

rows.law: Return a distinct hashtable carrying the same associations. If mutable-flag is absent or false, result is immutable; if true result is mutable. Subsequent association edits in mutable copy do not change original table.
positive_witnesses: Copy of mutable {1↦one, 2↦two} with no second argument has both associations and hashtable-mutable? false; source stays mutable.
Copy with explicit true has hashtable-mutable? true; set! copy[1]=changed leaves original[1]=one.
falsifiers: A default copy accepts mutation or is reported mutable.
Mutating explicit-mutable copy changes an original association or losing mappings during copy.
rows.dedup_basis: Exact lower and D10 name absent at pinned snapshot; semantic equivalence to any general copy+freeze operation not proven.
rows.ownership_question: Is default-immutable copied map a universal observable law, or a derived library function from D10 map constructors and capability flags?

rows.law: Return a boolean describing whether mutation of the hashtable is permitted; two tables with equal associations can differ in mutable state.
positive_witnesses: Immutable default copy and explicit mutable copy have equal initial mappings, but mutability predicates return false versus true.
falsifiers: Result is inferred exclusively from hashtable contents or size, so equal-association mutable/immutable instances are indistinguishable.
A default immutable copy is reported mutable.
rows.dedup_basis: Exact lower and D10 name absent at pinned snapshot; possibility of deriving from representation flag must be separately checked.
rows.ownership_question: Is mutability an independently observable table capability in the global semantics, or representation metadata requiring no Core resident?

admission.post_oracle_next_gate: Owner semantic dedup and arbitration via #4463/#4013, then serialized canonical-inventory selection under #4867; no automatic mutation.
